name: accumulate
title: accumulate(f, initial, xs) -> value
description: Applies binary function f to the elements of xs from right-to-left order, first applying f to the last element and the value initial, resulting in r1, then to the second-last element and r1, resulting in r2, etc, and finally to the first element and rn-1, where n is the length of the list. Thus, accumulate(f,zero,list(1,2,3)) results in f(1, f(2, f(3, zero))). Iterative process; time: Theta(n) (apart from f), space: Theta(n) (apart from f), where n is the length of xs.

name: append
title: append(xs, ys) -> list
description: Returns a list that results from appending the list ys to the list xs. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(n), where n is the length of xs. In the result, null at the end of the first argument list is replaced by the second argument, regardless what the second argument consists of.

name: build_list
title: build_list(f, n) -> list
description: Makes a list with n elements by applying the unary function f to the numbers 0 to n - 1, assumed to be a nonnegative integer. Iterative process; time: Theta(n) (apart from f), space: Theta(n) (apart from f).

name: display_list
title: display_list(xs, s) -> value
description: Optional second argument. Similar to display, but formats well-formed lists nicely if detected; time, space: Theta(n), where n is the total number of data structures such as pairs in x.

name: draw_data
title: draw_data(value1,value2,...,value_n) -> value
description: visualizes the arguments in a separate drawing area in the Source Academy using box-and-pointer diagrams; time, space: Theta(n), where n is the total number of data structures such as pairs in the arguments.

name: enum_list
title: enum_list(start, end) -> list
description: Returns a list that enumerates numbers starting from start using a step size of 1, until the number exceeds (>) end. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(n), where n is end - start.

name: equal
title: equal(x, y) -> boolean
description: Returns true if both have the same structure with respect to pair, and identical values at corresponding leave positions (places that are not themselves pairs), and false otherwise. For the "identical", the values need to have the same type, otherwise the result is false. If corresponding leaves are boolean values, these values need to be the same. If both are undefined or both are null, the result is true. Otherwise they are compared with === (using the definition of === in the respective JavaScript sublanguage in use). Time, space: Theta(n), where n is the total number of data structures such as pairs in x and y.

name: filter
title: filter(pred, xs) -> list
description: Returns a list that contains only those elements for which the one-argument function pred returns true. Iterative process; time: Theta(n) (apart from pred), space: Theta(n) (apart from pred), where n is the length of xs.

name: for_each
title: for_each(f, xs) -> boolean
description: Applies unary function f to every element of the list xs. Iterative process; time: Theta(n) (apart from f), space: Theta(1) (apart from f), where n is the length of xs. f is applied element-by-element: for_each(fun, list(1, 2)) results in the calls fun(1) and fun(2).

name: head
title: head(p) -> value
description: **primitive**; returns head (first component) of given pair p; time: Theta(1)Theta(1).

name: is_list
title: is_list(xs) -> xs
description: **primitive**; returns true if xs is a list as defined in the textbook, and false otherwise. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(1), where n is the length of the chain of tail operations that can be applied to xs. is_list recurses down the list and checks that it ends with the empty list null

name: is_null
title: is_null(x) -> boolean
description: **primitive**; returns true if x is the empty list null, and false otherwise; time: Theta(1)Theta(1).

name: is_pair
title: is_pair(x) -> boolean
description: **primitive**; returns true if x is a pair and false otherwise; time: Theta(1)Theta(1).

name: length
title: length(xs) -> number
description: Returns the length of the list xs. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(1), where n is the length of xs.

name: list
title: list(value1,value2,...,value_n) -> list
description: **primitive**; given n values, returns a list of length n. The elements of the list are the given values in the given order; time: Theta(n)Theta(n).

name: list_ref
title: list_ref(xs, n) -> value
description: Returns the element of list xs at position n, where the first element has index 0. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(1), where n is the length of xs.

name: list_to_string
title: list_to_string(xs) -> string
description: Returns a string that represents list xs using the text-based box-and-pointer notation [...]. Iterative process; time: Theta(n) where n is the size of the list, space: Theta(m) where m is the length of the string. The process is iterative, but consumes space O(m) because of the result string.

name: map
title: map(f, xs) -> list
description: Returns a list that results from list xs by element-wise application of unary function f. Iterative process; time: Theta(n) (apart from f), space: Theta(n) (apart from f), where n is the length of xs. f is applied element-by-element: map(f, list(1, 2)) results in list(f(1), f(2)).

name: member
title: member(v, xs) -> list
description: Returns first postfix sublist whose head is identical to v (using ===); returns null if the element does not occur in the list. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(1), where n is the length of xs.

name: pair
title: pair(x, y) -> pair
description: **primitive**; makes a pair whose head (first component) is x and whose tail (second component) is y; time: Theta(1)Theta(1).

name: remove
title: remove(v, xs) -> list
description: Returns a list that results from xs by removing the first item from xs that is identical (===) to v. Returns the original list if there is no occurrence. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(n), where n is the length of xs.

name: remove_all
title: remove_all(v, xs) -> list
description: Returns a list that results from xs by removing all items from xs that are identical (===) to v. Returns the original list if there is no occurrence. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(n), where n is the length of xs.

name: reverse
title: reverse(xs) -> list
description: Returns list xs in reverse order. Iterative process; time: Theta(n), space: Theta(n), where n is the length of xs. The process is iterative, but consumes space Theta(n) because of the result list.

name: tail
title: tail(p) -> value
description: **primitive**; returns tail (second component of given pair p; time: Theta(1)Theta(1).
